$comment: Behaviour that the Discovery document cannot express.
Every override carries provenance. Where Google's own documents disagree, the conflict is
recorded rather than silently resolved.

defaults.$comment: Per-operation entries below override these defaults.

health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.reconc.rationale: reconcile is a GET that returns a merged view; it has no server-side side effects.

health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.rollUp.scopeNote: Discovery revision 20260826 added the seven writeonly scopes to this read operation; the per-method reference still lists the readonly ones only, and omits none that Discovery has. The union is recorded because the two Google sources each omit scopes the other lists, and an accepted-scope list only causes harm when it is too small: a provider cannot select a token it is not told about. Verified against the per-method page on 2026-08-31.
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.rollUp.rationale: POST is used to carry a request body, but the operation only aggregates existing data. Page size and page token live in the request body, not the query string.
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.rollUp.pageSizeNote: pageSize does not bound the response: a request returning 1,686 points returns the same 1,686 with pageSize set to 1440, and the count was unchanged across eleven shapes and four data types. It bounds the query instead. The ceiling is floor(range cap / window) — whole windows that fit the data type's cap — and the check ignores the range requested, so a one-day request is refused on the same boundary as a ninety-day one. Boundaries land on that value exactly, including for windows that do not divide the cap, and the rule holds for both the 90-day and the 14-day types. The refusal is INVALID_ROLLUP_QUERY_DURATION, which names the duration rather than the field at fault. Left unset, the service behaves as though pageSize were ceil(range / window), and that implied value is subject to the same ceiling — so a range needing more windows than the cap allows is refused with nothing set. Measured against the live service on 2026-08-21.

health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.dailyR.scopeNote: Discovery revision 20260826 added the seven writeonly scopes to this read operation; the per-method reference still lists the readonly ones only, and omits none that Discovery has. The union is recorded because the two Google sources each omit scopes the other lists, and an accepted-scope list only causes harm when it is too small: a provider cannot select a token it is not told about. Verified against the per-method page on 2026-08-31.
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.dailyR.rationale: DailyRollUpDataPointsRequest declares pageSize and pageToken, but DailyRollUpDataPointsResponse has no nextPageToken. The generator must therefore NOT emit an EnumerateAsync overload for this operation.
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.dailyR.conflict: Request is paginated but the response provides no continuation token. Re-check on every Discovery revision bump; if a nextPageToken appears, switch kind to "body".
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.dailyR.pageSizeNote: pageSize does not bound the response: a request returning 1,686 points returns the same 1,686 with pageSize set to 1440, and the count was unchanged across eleven shapes and four data types. It bounds the query instead. The ceiling is floor(range cap / window) — whole windows that fit the data type's cap — and the check ignores the range requested, so a one-day request is refused on the same boundary as a ninety-day one. Boundaries land on that value exactly, including for windows that do not divide the cap, and the rule holds for both the 90-day and the 14-day types. The refusal is INVALID_ROLLUP_QUERY_DURATION, which names the duration rather than the field at fault. Left unset, the service behaves as though pageSize were ceil(range / window), and that implied value is subject to the same ceiling — so a range needing more windows than the cap allows is refused with nothing set. Measured against the live service on 2026-08-21. dailyRollUp additionally requires pageSize to be at least ceil(range / window), refusing smaller values as INVALID_DATA_POINT_NAME — again not the field at fault. The two bounds round in opposite directions: the ceiling truncates, the floor counts a partial window as a window, so twenty days of seven-day windows requires 3 and ten days of three-day windows requires 4. The floor counts windows and not days: eighty-four days of seven-day windows accepts 12 and rejects 84. Because the bounds are independent, a range needing more windows than the cap allows leaves no accepted value and cannot be requested. rollUp has no floor, so there an explicit pageSize within the ceiling is the way to request such a range.

health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.export.rationale: Discovery declares supportsMediaDownload=true AND a JSON response schema (ExportExerciseTcxResponse.tcxData). Both forms are real, so the generator emits a stream-first overload (alt=media) and a JSON overload. Treating this as media-only would discard the typed response.
health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.export.scopeNote: Discovery lists these two scopes as a flat array, which by convention means any one of them suffices. For this method the convention is wrong. The per-method reference carries an explicit note: "While the Authorization section below states that any one of the listed scopes is accepted, this specific method requires the user to provide both one of the activity_and_fitness scopes (normal or readonly) AND one of the location scopes (normal or readonly) in their access token to succeed." That page outranks Discovery under the source precedence in docs/architecture.md, so allOf is recorded here. The note's "normal" variants do not exist: neither Discovery nor the Scopes guide declares an unsuffixed googlehealth scope, and the only alternative to each readonly scope is a writeonly one, which cannot authorize a read. Both readonly scopes together is therefore the only combination the note can describe. An earlier draft declared this allOf and retracted it on 2026-08-10 as an assumption. The retraction was sound for the sources consulted then, which were Discovery and the REST index; it was reinstated on 2026-08-12 after reading the per-method page that states it outright.
integrationTestRequired: whether useMediaDownloadService=true implies a /download/ URL prefix

sources.note: States the activity-and-fitness AND location requirement that Discovery cannot express. Highest precedence source under docs/architecture.md.

health.users.dataTypes.dataPoints.patch.rationale: Unlike the other PATCH operations in this API, dataPoints.patch declares no updateMask parameter. The errors catalog documents UPDATE_ONLY_UPSERT_SUPPORTED, which suggests upsert semantics.

health.projects.subscribers.subscription.rationale: Subscriptions are NOT long-running: create and patch return Subscription directly and delete returns Empty. This asymmetry with the Subscriber resource is intentional in the wire contract and must not be normalised away.

$comment: Resource path segments collapsed away in the C# surface, so that callers write
client.Users.DataPoints rather than client.Users.DataTypes.DataPoints.
dataTypes declares no methods of its own: the data type is selected by the parent
resource name, for example users/me/dataTypes/heart-rate. projects also declares no
methods but is NOT flattened, because it is a real namespace in the public surface.
This is an explicit list rather than a heuristic so the API shape stays reviewable.
Discovery revision 20260826 contains 147 schemas; 138 are reachable from the allowlisted
operations. Without pruning the generator would emit dead types such as HttpBody,
ManifestParams, DateTime, TimeZone, HttpHeader and HttpResponse.
Discovery supplies the scope list; the per-method REST reference outranks it where the two
disagree, which is the source precedence docs/architecture.md already declares. The Scopes
guide is a cross-check only. Compared on 2026-08-10, Discovery and the guide disagree in
both directions, which is why the rule exists.
A Discovery scopes array carries no combination, and the convention that any one entry
suffices holds everywhere except dataPoints.exportExerciseTcx, whose per-method page says an
activity-and-fitness scope and a location scope are both required. That operation declares
allOf; every other operation is anyOf. Re-read the per-method pages on a revision bump, not
just Discovery: this exception is invisible from Discovery alone.

inScopesGuideOnly.note: Declared by no operation in Discovery revision 20260826, but listed by the Scopes guide AND by the per-method reference of every read operation that returns data points. It was previously not generated, on the grounds that no operation accepted it; that conclusion came from reading Discovery alone. It is now generated from additionalScopes below.

inPerMethodReferenceOnly.note: Discovery revision 20260826 withdrew this scope from auth.oauth2.scopes and from every operation that declared it. The per-method reference for dataPoints create, patch and batchDelete still lists it on 2026-08-31, and architecture.md gives that reference precedence. It was previously in inDiscoveryOnly, generated from the snapshot; it is now generated from additionalScopes below, the same way nutrition.readonly is. Withdrawing the constant would be a breaking change made on one source of two while the other still documents the scope as accepted.

authentication.$comment: These use project/IAM credentials (cloud-platform), not end-user OAuth.

$comment: What a scope grants, which Discovery states in prose and not in a field. Read from the
description on each scope: Google writes 'See your Google Health X data' for one that
reads and 'Add X data to Google Health, and edit or delete the data it adds.' for one
that writes. Listed here rather than derived at generation time, because a rule over the
text would be a rule over Google's copywriting.
Not derivable from the operations either, measured on 2026-08-15: five .readonly scopes
are declared by POST operations - rollUp, dailyRollUp and reconcile are POSTs that read -
so 'appears on a mutating method' classifies them as writes. The suffix and the HTTP
method disagree in 5 of 19 cases; the description agrees with the suffix in all 19.
Generation fails if a scope in Discovery is missing from these lists, so a scope Google
adds is a build failure rather than a scope that silently belongs to no kind.
Includes the scopes semantics.json adds under scopeCrossCheck.additionalScopes, which are generated alongside Discovery's own and would otherwise be unclassified.
Which schemas are unions, and which of their message-typed members are not alternatives.
Discovery has no way to say 'exactly one of these', so the shape is inferred; without this
the generator treats every $ref property as a member and the first one alphabetically wins.

DataPoint.roundTripNote: Reading a data point and sending it back is what dataPoints.patch is, so a member dropped on the way in would be removed from a person's record on the way out.
DataPoint.rationale: dataSource is metadata carried by every data point, not one of the things a data point can be. Google: "Data Source definition to track the origin of data. Each health data point, regardless of the complexity or data model (whether a simple step count or a detailed sleep session) must retain information about its source of origin." It sorts before heartRate, sleep and steps, so including it made GetKind() return DataSource for every real measurement. It stays a normal property; only the union helpers ignore it.

RollupDataPoint.roundTripNote: Roll-ups are computed by the service and never sent back to it, so nothing can be lost from a person's record this way. What is at stake is the caller's own copy: a member dropped here would be missing from whatever it stores or forwards.
RollupDataPoint.rationale: All 21 message-typed members are measurements; this schema has no dataSource.

DailyRollupDataPoint.roundTripNote: Roll-ups are computed by the service and never sent back to it, so nothing can be lost from a person's record this way. What is at stake is the caller's own copy: a member dropped here would be missing from whatever it stores or forwards.
DailyRollupDataPoint.rationale: The window this row aggregates over, not something aggregated. Both are CivilDateTime and both sort before every measurement, so including them would make GetKind() answer civilEndTime for every daily roll-up — the same failure dataSource caused on DataPoint. They stay normal properties; the caller needs them to know which day the row is.
